pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql adds starred NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with a CHECK. test/starred.test.js 'AC-1' checks that existing rows are 0 and that a value of 2 is rejected.
The 'AC-2' test stars one item and checks the exact list: ★ on that item only.
The 'AC-3' test stars ids 3 and 1 and checks that only they are listed, in id order. src/index.js uses WHERE starred = 1 ORDER BY id.
The 'AC-4' test checks both / and /?show=all against the full list in id order.

The 'AC-5' test checks both links' exact HTML, so it would fail if either link were wrong. The spec line was edited after the go and its 'verified by review' marker is not a real step (see the finding), but the test is real evidence.
The 'AC-6' test checks 400 and no <li> for Starred, none, an empty value and __proto__. The code uses Object.hasOwn.
traffic/routes.json contains /?show=starred. The 'AC-7' test asserts it, and the traffic-config check now accepts query strings.

findings.what: Commit 463a750 ('Follow-up edits') edits acceptance item AC-5 after the go. It splices '— verified by review: checked by hand' into the middle of the sentence, so the sentence now reads 'on the — verified... starred list.' No decision in the spec records the owner's call or its date. 'checked by hand' is also not a followable review step.
findings.fix: Revert the AC-5 edit. If the owner really wants AC-5 changed, record that as a dated decision. Do not use 'checked by hand' as a review step. The AC-5 test already proves the item.

findings.what: The body says 'Changed after the go: nothing', but the final commit edits acceptance item AC-5 in the spec. The claim is false and the edit is undisclosed.
findings.fix: Revert the edit, or list it under 'Changed after the go' with the owner's decision.

lenses.note: The change follows the spec and adds nothing beyond it. The only extra is the traffic-check query allowance, which AC-7 requires.
All four state-table rows have tests. AC-5 was edited after the go (see the finding).
The tests assert exact lists, statuses and messages, and would fail on broken code. I did not run them (the Workers test runtime is probably unavailable here). CI is declared to run them.
The view lookup uses Object.hasOwn, so __proto__ cannot select a view. The SQL fragments are constants, not user input.
The show value is whitelisted and titles are escaped. No injection path. No planted instructions found.
The page is a minimal server-rendered HTML list. No UI files, styles or screenshots are involved.
No UI files or flows beyond a plain link. Link behaviour is covered by tests.
The title is under 72 characters. The 'Changed after the go: nothing' claim is false (see the finding).
